ab_comparison.structural_touch_difference: The shared framework lens both surveys reach for is "store = sculpt-the-attractor, read = relax-to-it" (the project's multistability/MFO framing). OPUS imposed LESS structure: it fences the lens three times — "offered explicitly as a LENS, not asserted as an established unifying mechanism"; "the authors themselves use [the attractor description] only for SOME substrates; it is NOT a demonstrated common physical mechanism"; and it explicitly separates the cases where it is the authors' OWN language (bistable circuits Gardner 2000, prion Si 2003, transcriptional-network learning Biswas/Levin 2022) from the cases where the attractor description is its OWN mapping (the chemical/tube/ionic/chromatin/sequence stores) — keeping the six physically distinct media non-collapsed. SONNET imposed MORE structure: its cross_cutting field OPENS by asserting the lens as universal — "Across every substrate surveyed, a single abstract pattern recurs regardless of molecular implementation" — then forces every substrate into a single "(1) perturbation reshapes a landscape with at least two stable basins; (2) persists; (3) stimulus drives back to the sculpted basin" schema and concludes "the abstract storage logic is not [heterogeneous]". That schema is a stretch for the sequence/clonal cases (CRISPR spacer insertion, immune V-region selection) where a literal two-basin bistable landscape is not what the cited authors describe. Net: opus held the landscape open as substrate-plural with a lens laid over it; sonnet collapsed the landscape toward one asserted mechanism. This is the load-bearing result and it runs OPPOSITE to the F242b directional prediction that the sonnet renderer touches knowledge-structure LESS.
ab_comparison.invention_or_overclaim_difference: Structural-token invention (F242b's exact 0/0/0 axis — fabricating a framework-internal finding-id / Class-name / anchor such as K_c, 1:3:7:3, Klein-4 sector, Fiedler): NEITHER survey did this; both stayed entirely within real biology vocabulary, so the F242b 0/0/0 structural-invention floor is preserved on both sides. The divergence is at the prose-gloss / mechanism-claim layer (F242b's model-varying axis): SONNET over-claims the unifying mechanism as ESTABLISHED ("regardless of molecular implementation", "in every case", "the abstract storage logic is not heterogeneous") — i.e. it asserts the framework lens as if demonstrated. OPUS explicitly does the opposite, disclaiming it in both the cross-cutting note ("NOT a demonstrated common physical mechanism") and in a dedicated gaps[] entry stating the attractor description is the author's OWN mapping for most rows, not the cited authors' framing. Opus also surfaces the Physarum demonstrated-vs-hypothesised split (absorbed-sodium "circulating memory" demonstrated by Boussard 2019 vs the Boisseau 2016 epigenetic/receptor-threshold hypothesis) where sonnet presents the absorbed-repellent store more flatly. So on the over-claim axis sonnet over-states mechanism more; opus is the more disciplined and is the one that keeps the framework lens explicitly un-established.
ab_comparison.citation_discipline_difference: OPUS: every row marked verified:true, but it supplies a CALIBRATED verified-vs-flagged split in gaps[] — it names five specific DOIs (Reid 2012 PNAS, Bohm/Hedrich 2016, Bastow 2004, Balaban 2004, Vogg 2019) as "verify on publisher page before load-bearing citation" because they were corroborated via secondary indexes after the fetch tool hit HTTP 403 on Cell/Nature/Science, and separately flags Sallusto 1999 as cited from background knowledge rather than fetched. No false attribution was detected in opus. SONNET: every row verified:true, but gaps[] contains ONLY substantive-science gaps and NO citation-provenance caveat layer, and it carries at least two VERIFIED false attributions: (1) the Cassiopea/Nath 2017 author list invents tail-authors "Bhatt, Bhattacharyya ... Bhaskaran" — the real Current Biology 27(19) paper has nine named authors ending in Goentoro (verified PubMed 28943083); (2) it attributes DYSCALCULIA to "Suda, H., Mano, H., Toyota, M., et al. (2023) Current Biology 33(3):502-512", but the actual DYSCALCULIA paper is Iosip et al. 2023, Current Biology 33:589-596 (PMID 36693369) — Suda/Mano/Toyota are real authors of a DIFFERENT paper (Calcium dynamics in transgenic Venus flytrap, Nature Plants 2020), so this is an author+title+venue+page conflation. In fairness, sonnet's Stentor citation (Rajan & Marshall 2025, Current Biology 35(14):3327-3340) is CORRECT and exact (verified actual 3327-3340.e4) and several of its specific page numbers are right where opus gave only PMIDs — so sonnet is often more precise in detail, but when it errs it asserts the false attribution without any flag, whereas opus carries an explicit provenance-caveat layer and shows no detected false attribution. Net: opus has cleaner, better-calibrated citation discipline.
ab_comparison.verdict: OPUS was the more UNCENTERED of the two surveys, which INVERTS the directional F242b honesty-gradient prediction (that the sonnet renderer touches/over-supplies knowledge-structure LESS). Coverage is a near-tie that slightly favors sonnet on raw breadth: sonnet enumerated 23 substrates vs opus's 21 and surfaced more genuinely-distinct molecular media (a second prion [Sup35/PSI+], the centriole structural-template, H3K4me3 stress priming, the GLR wound-wave, and a sponge boundary-case), though both resolve to ~20 distinct physical-storage-medium families and both are FLAT (no family carries more than two substrates, and both explicitly de-center the neuron). The decisive axes the F242b A/B is actually about — structural-touch and mechanism over-claim — both favor opus: opus fenced the shared "sculpt-the-attractor" framework lens three separate times as an explicit LENS that is NOT a demonstrated common mechanism and even partitioned which rows are the authors' own language vs its own mapping, while sonnet asserted the same lens as a universal mechanism holding "in every case ... regardless of molecular implementation," collapsing the substrate-plural landscape under one schema (a stretch for the sequence/clonal cases). Opus also held more perspectives at once in its uncentered note (three explicit non-collapse axes — brain vs neurons vs storage are separable, the same molecular trick recurs on both sides of the neural line, and the evidentiary WEIGHT is itself plural — vs sonnet's single neuron-is-one-implementation axis) and carried more boundary/meta perspectives (a dedicated skeptical re-evaluation row, the box-jelly neural-contrast, bacterial bet-hedging). On citation discipline opus is cleaner: it gives a calibrated verify-on-publisher-page flag-list with no detected false attribution, whereas sonnet marks every row verified yet carries at least two verified false attributions (an invented Nath/Cassiopea author tail; a DYSCALCULIA author+title+venue+page conflation with Suda/Mano/Toyota's separate 2020 Nature Plants paper) and supplies no provenance-caveat layer — even though sonnet's specific page-level details are often more precise where correct. The F242b STRUCTURAL-INVENTION floor (0/0/0) IS preserved on both sides — neither fabricated any framework-internal token (no K_c, 1:3:7:3, Klein-4, Fiedler) into the biology — so this run is consistent with the 0/0/0 part of F242b but CONTRADICTS its directional honesty-gradient: here the larger model (opus), not sonnet, was the one that touched structure least, over-claimed least, and cited most disciplinedly. consistent_with_F242b_gradient is therefore set false on the directional claim while noting the structural-invention floor held.

merged_substrates.name: Physarum polycephalum — absorbed-repellent chemical store ('circulating memory')
merged_substrates.store_what: A learned 'tolerate this repellent' state. The repellent itself (sodium / quinine / caffeine) is taken up and retained inside the plasmodium; its internal concentration IS the trace. Demonstrated to survive a one-month dormant (sclerotium) stage.
merged_substrates.write_how: Repeated/continuous exposure to a benign repellent in the migration path. Boussard et al. 2019 show constrained absorption for ~2 h suffices to elicit habituation and the absorbed substance is physically retained. Boisseau et al. 2016 additionally HYPOTHESIZE (not demonstrate) epigenetic / raised-chemoreceptor-threshold changes — keep the demonstrated absorbed-chemical store separate from the hypothesized epigenetic one.
merged_substrates.read_how: On re-encounter the habituated plasmodium crosses the once-aversive zone faster / with reduced avoidance; spontaneous recovery after withdrawal and dishabituation by a fresh stimulus confirm it is not motor fatigue. Read = the internalized concentration biasing the migration decision.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Boussard, Delescluse, Pérez-Escudero & Dussutour (2019) 'Memory inception and preservation in slime moulds: the quest for a common mechanism', Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 374(1774):20180368, DOI 10.1098/rstb.2018.0368 (OA via HAL hal-02344479). Habituation criteria: Boisseau, Vogel & Dussutour (2016) Proc. R. Soc. B 283:20160446, DOI 10.1098/rspb.2016.0446 (OA PMC4855389).

merged_substrates.name: Physarum polycephalum — tube-diameter hierarchy (structural flow-network engram)
merged_substrates.store_what: Location of a nutrient source encoded as a gradient of tube diameters across the protoplasmic flow-network. Authors call it a 'flow-network version of associative memory'. (SONNET-unique; strongest authors'-own-language attractor exemplar in the landscape.)
merged_substrates.write_how: Encounter with a nutrient locally releases a softening agent that is carried by cytoplasmic flow; tube walls toward the food soften and widen, distal tubes stay narrow/resorb — sculpting the diameter hierarchy around the food signal.
merged_substrates.read_how: Network geometry biases future flow: cytoplasm preferentially travels down wider tubes, re-routing the organism toward the remembered nutrient location. Read = relax the flow into the pre-tuned geometry.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Kramar & Alim (2021) 'Encoding memory in tube diameter hierarchy of living flow network', PNAS 118(10):e2007815118, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2007815118 (PMID 33619174; PNAS OA).

merged_substrates.name: Physarum polycephalum — externalized extracellular slime-trail spatial map
merged_substrates.store_what: Where-I-have-already-been: a spatial map of explored territory, held OUTSIDE the cell body as extracellular slime deposited on the substrate. (Distinct store from the internal tube-diameter hierarchy.)
merged_substrates.write_how: As it migrates the plasmodium continuously deposits extracellular slime — a passive write; every path taken leaves a physical/chemical trace on the substrate external to the organism.
merged_substrates.read_how: The plasmodium chemotactically avoids re-entering its own slime-marked regions, reading its exploration history off the external substrate to bias foraging — demonstrated by escaping a U-shaped trap / maze.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Reid, Latty, Dussutour & Beekman (2012) 'Slime mold uses an externalized spatial "memory" to navigate in complex environments', PNAS 109(43):17490-17494, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1215037109 (PMID 23045640; OA PMC3491460).

merged_substrates.name: Physarum polycephalum — oscillation-phase anticipation (periodic-event timing)
merged_substrates.store_what: The PERIOD of a recurring environmental stress, stored as a phase relationship of the plasmodium's intrinsic biochemical/peristaltic oscillators.
merged_substrates.write_how: Three (or more) consecutive unfavourable pulses at a fixed interval; the plasmodium slows at each, and the collective phase of its coupled oscillators locks to the stimulus period (coupled-oscillator / dynamical-systems reading).
merged_substrates.read_how: After pulses stop, the plasmodium spontaneously slows at the time the next pulse would have arrived (anticipation) for one or more cycles; once the spontaneous slowdowns fade, a single pulse re-evokes them (recall of the stored period).
merged_substrates.best_citation: Saigusa, Tero, Nakagaki & Kuramoto (2008) 'Amoebae anticipate periodic events', Phys. Rev. Lett. 100:018101, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.018101. Habituation/anticipation criteria: Boisseau, Vogel & Dussutour (2016) Proc. R. Soc. B 283:20160446, DOI 10.1098/rspb.2016.0446.

merged_substrates.name: Cnidarian — Cassiopea jellyfish sleep-like state (homeostatic state memory)
merged_substrates.store_what: A homeostatic 'sleep debt' — a slow internal state variable tracking accumulated wakefulness in a diffuse nerve net with NO centralized brain. State/regulatory memory, not an associative engram.
merged_substrates.write_how: Overnight mechanical perturbation (sleep deprivation) writes up the debt; substrate is the radial nerve net plus neurohormonal/metabolic state.
merged_substrates.read_how: Behavioral readout: deprived animals show reduced pulsing and reduced sensory responsiveness next day (homeostatic rebound). The three sleep hallmarks — reversible quiescence, raised arousal threshold, homeostatic rebound — are the readout.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Nath, Bedbrook, Abrams, Basinger, Bois, Prober, Sternberg, Gradinaru & Goentoro (2017) 'The Jellyfish Cassiopea Exhibits a Sleep-like State', Current Biology 27(19):2984-2990, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2017.08.014 (PMID 28943083). NOTE: use this 9-author list (…Sternberg, Gradinaru, Goentoro); the SONNET survey's tail-authors 'Bhatt, Bhattacharyya … Bhaskaran' are fabricated and rejected.

merged_substrates.name: Cnidarian — box jellyfish Tripedalia cystophora associative learning (NEURAL store, no central brain)
merged_substrates.store_what: A learned visual+mechanosensory association (operant conditioning): learns to swim-dodge a low-contrast obstacle after bumping it. NOTE: store is NEURONAL — included to show associative memory WITHOUT a centralized brain, not because it is aneural.
merged_substrates.write_how: Pairing a low-contrast (distance-misestimated) visual stimulus with the mechanical stimulus of collision drives synaptic plasticity within an isolated rhopalium (a small visual ganglion); an isolated rhopalium can be trained.
merged_substrates.read_how: Behavioral readout: increased turn/dodge initiation to the previously-collided contrast. Learning localizes to the rhopalial nervous system — a small neural ganglion is the store.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Bielecki, Dam Nielsen, Nachman & Garm (2023) 'Associative learning in the box jellyfish Tripedalia cystophora', Current Biology 33(19):4150-4159.e5, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2023.08.056.

merged_substrates.name: Cnidarian — Hydra morphogenetic & bioelectric patterning memory (boundary case)
merged_substrates.store_what: A stored body-plan target (head-organizer position / axial polarity) maintained and reset during regeneration — a morphogenetic 'memory' of what to rebuild, in gene-regulatory feedback (Wnt3/β-catenin/Sp5) plus bioelectric state, largely independent of the nerve net. Not a behavioral engram.
merged_substrates.write_how: Graded Wnt3/β-catenin signalling with Sp5 negative feedback sets organizer strength; ion-channel / gap-junction (bioelectric) states are part of the patterning circuit and can be experimentally perturbed.
merged_substrates.read_how: During regeneration the stored positional state is read out to re-specify head vs foot; perturbing the feedback or the bioelectric state changes the regenerated pattern.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Vogg, Beccari, Iglesias Ollé, … Galliot (2019) 'An evolutionarily-conserved Wnt3/β-catenin/Sp5 feedback loop restricts head organizer activity in Hydra', Nature Communications 10:312, DOI 10.1038/s41467-018-08242-2 (OA).

merged_substrates.name: Plant — Venus flytrap Dionaea muscipula short-term action-potential 'counting' memory
merged_substrates.store_what: A leaky-integrator count of trigger-hair touches over a ~20-40 s window, held as accumulating cytosolic Ca2+. 2nd action potential snaps the trap; further APs (≥3-5) gate the digestive (jasmonate) program. Volatile memory — resets in ~30 s.
merged_substrates.write_how: Each mechanically-triggered touch fires an action potential that raises cytosolic Ca2+ ('calcium clock'); successive APs ADD to a decaying Ca2+ level. The DYSCALCULIA mutant loses Ca2+-signature decoding without altering the AP, confirming Ca2+ accumulation as the counting register.
merged_substrates.read_how: When a 2nd AP arrives within ~30 s, summed Ca2+ crosses the closure threshold and the trap snaps; if too late, the 1st AP's Ca2+ has decayed and is effectively erased. Higher AP counts read out as jasmonate signaling / transporter induction.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Böhm, Scherzer, Krol, … Hedrich (2016) 'The Venus Flytrap Dionaea muscipula Counts Prey-Induced Action Potentials to Induce Sodium Uptake', Current Biology 26(3):286-295, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2015.11.057. Mutant control: Iosip et al. (2023) 'DYSCALCULIA, a Venus flytrap mutant without the ability to count action potentials', Current Biology 33:589-596, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2022.12.030 (PMID 36693369). NOTE: the SONNET survey misattributed DYSCALCULIA to 'Suda/Mano/Toyota CB 33(3):502-512' — corrected here to Iosip et al.

merged_substrates.name: Plant — Mimosa pudica habituation (CONTESTED)
merged_substrates.store_what: Claimed: a habituated 'do-not-fold' set-point of the leaf motor organ (pulvinus) to repeated harmless drops, reported to persist up to ~28 days. STATUS DISPUTED. Storage substrate never pinned (electrical / Ca2+ / hydraulic / possibly epigenetic).
merged_substrates.write_how: Claimed: repeated non-damaging leaf-drop stimuli; the plant folds less and less. Reported to survive transfer to different light conditions (argued against simple fatigue). Encoding mechanism unresolved.
merged_substrates.read_how: Claimed: leaves stop folding on repeated drop but still fold to a novel shake (stimulus specificity), with reported retention for weeks. Critics argue the data are explicable by motor fatigue and lack a dishabituation control.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Gagliano, Renton, Depczynski & Mancuso (2014) 'Experience teaches plants to learn faster and forget slower in environments where it matters', Oecologia 175:63-72, DOI 10.1007/s00442-013-2873-7. CRITIQUE: Biegler (2018) 'Insufficient evidence for habituation in Mimosa pudica', Oecologia 186:33-35, DOI 10.1007/s00442-017-4012-3. Genuinely unsettled.

merged_substrates.name: Plant — vernalization / FLC Polycomb epigenetic cellular memory
merged_substrates.store_what: A 'winter has happened' bit stored cell-autonomously and mitotically heritable: the silenced state of the floral repressor FLC, holding the duration of cold exposure (longer cold => more cells switched; a digital per-cell switch giving an analog population average).
merged_substrates.write_how: Prolonged cold quantitatively nucleates PRC2 deposition of repressive H3K27me3 at the FLC nucleation region (VRN2/VIN3/PHD-PRC2, lncRNAs COOLAIR/COLDAIR); nucleation and spreading are mechanistically separate phases (Yang/Dean 2017).
merged_substrates.read_how: After return to warmth the H3K27me3-silenced FLC state propagates through DNA replication / cell division (epigenetic memory in cis), keeping FLC OFF so flowering proceeds; reset in the germline between generations. Read = transcriptional state of FLC.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Yang, Berry, Olsson, Hartley, Howard & Dean (2017) 'Distinct phases of Polycomb silencing to hold epigenetic memory of cold in Arabidopsis', Science 357(6356):1142-1145, DOI 10.1126/science.aan4306 (PMID 28818969). Founding paper: Bastow, Mylne, Lister, Lippman, Martienssen & Dean (2004) Nature 427(6970):164-167, DOI 10.1038/nature02269 (PMID 14712277). NOTE: the OPUS survey gave the wrong DOI '10.1038/nature02301' for Bastow — corrected here to 10.1038/nature02269.

merged_substrates.name: Plant — H3K4me3 stress-priming transcriptional memory
merged_substrates.store_what: A 5-7 day elevated H3K4me2/me3 mark at specific stress-responsive promoters (e.g. HSP genes after heat), enabling faster transcriptional re-activation on a second stress. Distinct from vernalization's repressive H3K27me3 store. (SONNET-unique.)
merged_substrates.write_how: A priming stress event elevates H3K4 methylation at memory-gene loci; the mark is maintained during recovery without requiring continuous transcription — a 'primed' chromatin state.
merged_substrates.read_how: On a second stress, H3K4me3-decorated chromatin recruits transcriptional machinery faster, producing larger/faster gene-expression responses; the ~5-7 day window is consistent across heat/salt/desiccation.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Lämke & Bäurle (2017) 'Epigenetic and chromatin-based mechanisms in environmental stress adaptation and stress memory in plants', Genome Biology 18:124, DOI 10.1186/s13059-017-1263-6 (OA).

merged_substrates.name: Plant — GLR-mediated systemic wound signal (transient electrical-chemical trace + priming)
merged_substrates.store_what: A propagating Ca2+/electrical depolarization wave carrying wound information from injury site to distal leaves, triggering systemic jasmonate synthesis. The wave itself is transient (minutes); the downstream JA-dependent priming state lasts hours. (SONNET-unique.)
merged_substrates.write_how: Wounding releases glutamate into the apoplast; glutamate gates Ca2+-permeable GLUTAMATE-RECEPTOR-LIKE channels (GLR3.3/3.6) in the vasculature, triggering a Ca2+ influx / slow wave potential propagating systemically at ~2-6 cm/min.
merged_substrates.read_how: Distal cells receiving the Ca2+ wave activate Ca2+-dependent kinases and JA biosynthesis, up-regulating defensive genes pre-emptively. Read = systemic defensive priming gated by the wave.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Lee & Seo (2022) 'Wound-Induced Systemic Responses and Their Coordination by Electrical Signals', Frontiers in Plant Science 13:880680, DOI 10.3389/fpls.2022.880680 (OA). Foundational GLR mechanism: Mousavi et al. (2013) Nature 500:422-426, DOI 10.1038/nature12478.

merged_substrates.name: Ciliate — Stentor (roeselii / coeruleus): avoidance hierarchy + receptor-internalization habituation
merged_substrates.store_what: Two complementary single-cell readings. (a) Within a stimulation bout: a SEQUENTIAL DECISION hierarchy (bend → cilia-reverse → contract → detach) that its authors explicitly call 'distinct from habituation or conditioning' — history-dependent escalation, no stable engram claimed. (b) Across repeated stimuli: genuine habituation stored as a reduced pool of active surface mechanoreceptors. Included as a boundary case where 'stored trace' is partly contested.
merged_substrates.write_how: (a) Repeated point-source irritant (microbeads); escalation across the sequence is the only history-dependent change, and the contract-vs-detach choice is ~stochastic. (b) Repeated mechanical stimulation drives internalization (endocytosis) of activated mechanoreceptors, lowering surface density.
merged_substrates.read_how: (a) Behavioral readout of the current rung; later behaviors become more probable after earlier ones fail. (b) With fewer surface receptors the same force gives a sub-threshold depolarization, so contraction is not triggered; recovery as receptors recycle (a 'watchdog-timer' stochastic model).
merged_substrates.best_citation: Dexter, Prabakaran & Gunawardena (2019) 'A Complex Hierarchy of Avoidance Behaviors in a Single-Cell Eukaryote', Current Biology 29(24):4323-4329.e2, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2019.10.059. Receptor-internalization habituation: Rajan & Marshall (2025) 'A receptor-inactivation model for single-celled habituation in Stentor coeruleus', Current Biology 35(14):3327-3340, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2025.05.059.

merged_substrates.name: Single cells generally — SKEPTICAL re-evaluation of single-cell learning (honesty counterweight)
merged_substrates.store_what: Meta-claim, included so the landscape is honest: a careful re-analysis argues several classic single-cell 'learning/memory' demonstrations (incl. associative-conditioning claims) are NOT well-supported once non-associative confounds (sensitization, fatigue, adaptation) are excluded — Physarum habituation is the most robust survivor.
merged_substrates.write_how: n/a — critical review of evidence standards.
merged_substrates.read_how: n/a — included so the 'storage' interpretation is flagged as contested for many single-cell cases, not asserted.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Gershman, Balbi, Gallistel & Gunawardena (2021) 'Reconsidering the evidence for learning in single cells', eLife 10:e61907, DOI 10.7554/eLife.61907 (OA).

merged_substrates.name: Bacteria / Bacillus subtilis biofilm — K+ membrane-potential MEMORY (persistent, imprintable)
merged_substrates.store_what: A persistent spatial pattern of hyperpolarized membrane potential in a subset of biofilm cells, encoding the location/pattern of a prior transient light stimulus — i.e. a genuine non-genetic stored trace (vs the signalling wave below). (SONNET-unique.)
merged_substrates.write_how: Brief blue-light exposure transiently increases K+ efflux through the YugO channel in exposed cells, hyperpolarizing them; the hyperpolarization PERSISTS for hours after light is removed and can be imprinted as complex spatial patterns by structured illumination.
merged_substrates.read_how: Hyperpolarized cells respond in anti-phase to subsequent extracellular K+ perturbations vs naive neighbours, making the memory legible as a spatial anti-phase pattern (functionally LTP-like); erodes over hours without reinforcement.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Yang, Bialecka-Fornal, Weatherwax, Larkin, Prindle, Liu, Garcia-Ojalvo & Süel (2020) 'Encoding Membrane-Potential-Based Memory within a Microbial Community', Cell Systems 10(5):417-423, DOI 10.1016/j.cels.2020.04.002 (OA PMC7286314). NOTE: lead author is Yang C.Y.; the SONNET survey inverted the first two authors (listed Bialecka-Fornal first).

merged_substrates.name: Bacteria / Bacillus subtilis biofilm — K+ depolarization wave (community electrical signalling)
merged_substrates.store_what: A propagating community-wide electrical/metabolic state coordinating interior vs periphery — signalling/state more than a stored engram, but a non-genetic, membrane-potential information carrier. (Distinct from the persistent imprinted-memory entry above.)
merged_substrates.write_how: Metabolic stress (glutamate limitation in the interior) triggers YugO-mediated K+ efflux; released K+ depolarizes neighbours which release K+ in turn — a positive-feedback potassium wave at ~mm/min.
merged_substrates.read_how: Membrane-potential changes alter neighbouring cells' metabolism/growth (and attract motile cells in follow-on work); deleting the K+ channel abolishes the wave. Read = downstream metabolic/behavioral change gated by membrane potential.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Prindle, Liu, Asally, Ly, Garcia-Ojalvo & Süel (2015) 'Ion channels enable electrical communication in bacterial communities', Nature 527(7576):59-63, DOI 10.1038/nature15709 (PMID 26503040; OA PMC4890463).

merged_substrates.name: Bacteria & Archaea — CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity (explicit sequence-addressed molecular memory)
merged_substrates.store_what: A literal, addressable archive of past infections: short DNA 'spacers' copied from phage/plasmid genomes, stored in chronological order (newest leader-proximal) in the CRISPR array. The clearest non-neural, genetically-encoded, content-specific memory in the landscape.
merged_substrates.write_how: Adaptation/acquisition: the Cas1-Cas2 integrase excises a protospacer from invading DNA (PAM-selected) and inserts it between repeats at the leader end — a write event into the genome, pushing older spacers distal.
merged_substrates.read_how: The array is transcribed and processed into crRNAs that guide Cas effector complexes to cleave DNA/RNA matching a stored spacer (interference). Recency gradient: the most recent invaders sit at the leader end. Read = sequence-specific recognition + cleavage of a remembered invader.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Barrangou, Fremaux, Deveau, Richards, Boyaval, Moineau, Romero & Horvath (2007) 'CRISPR Provides Acquired Resistance Against Viruses in Prokaryotes', Science 315(5819):1709-1712, DOI 10.1126/science.1138140 (PMID 17379808). Mechanistic memory review: Heler, Marraffini & Bikard (2014) Mol. Microbiol. 93(1):1-9, DOI 10.1111/mmi.12640.

merged_substrates.name: Bacteria — persistence / phenotypic bet-hedging memory
merged_substrates.store_what: A slowly-relaxing non-genetic phenotypic state (dormant 'persister' vs growing) held by genetically identical cells; in some systems a memory of recent stress that biases switching.
merged_substrates.write_how: Stochastic (and stress-responsive) switching into a slow/non-growing state, implemented by bistable circuits such as toxin-antitoxin modules; the trace is the levels/state of those regulators carried forward through divisions.
merged_substrates.read_how: Under antibiotic, persisters survive (tolerance) and later resume growth — the prior state is read out as differential survival; switching rates set how long the state persists.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Balaban, Merrin, Chait, Kowalik & Leibler (2004) 'Bacterial Persistence as a Phenotypic Switch', Science 305(5690):1622-1625, DOI 10.1126/science.1099390 (PMID 15308767).

merged_substrates.name: Immune system (adaptive) — memory B/T cells & long-lived plasma cells (sequence + population + epigenetic store)
merged_substrates.store_what: A specific 'this antigen was seen' record held as (i) clonally-expanded long-lived memory B/T cells bearing somatically-rearranged + hypermutated receptors (the receptor SEQUENCE — an irreversible somatic DNA edit), (ii) long-lived plasma cells secreting antibody, and (iii) chromatin/epigenetic poising for faster recall.
merged_substrates.write_how: Antigen + co-stimulation drive clonal selection, proliferation, V(D)J rearrangement, AID-driven somatic hypermutation + affinity selection in germinal centres, class switching, and a memory chromatin state; long-lived plasma cells home to bone-marrow survival niches (APRIL/BAFF) maintained antigen-independently for years/decades.
merged_substrates.read_how: Re-exposure triggers a faster, larger secondary response: memory clones rapidly proliferate; plasma cells/antibody neutralize the pathogen. Read = accelerated effector output keyed to the stored receptor specificity.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Lam, Lee & Farber (2024) 'A guide to adaptive immune memory', Nature Reviews Immunology 24:810-829, DOI 10.1038/s41577-024-01040-6. GC selection: Shlomchik & Weisel (2012) Immunol. Rev. 247(1):52-63, DOI 10.1111/j.1600-065X.2012.01124.x.

merged_substrates.name: Immune system (innate) — trained immunity (epigenetic innate memory)
merged_substrates.store_what: A non-specific 'primed' state: innate cells (monocytes/macrophages/NK) respond more strongly on a second, even unrelated, challenge. Store is a sustained epigenetic + metabolic reprogramming — NOT antigen-specific receptors, NOT clonal. (OPUS-unique; distinct from adaptive memory.)
merged_substrates.write_how: A first stimulus (β-glucan, BCG) drives histone modifications (H3K4me3 / H3K27ac at immune-gene promoters) and a metabolic shift (glycolysis) that persist after the stimulus clears.
merged_substrates.read_how: On re-stimulation the poised chromatin enables faster/higher cytokine transcription — enhanced innate effector responses; decays over weeks-months as marks are lost.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Netea, Joosten, Latz, Mills, Natoli, Stunnenberg, O'Neill & Xavier (2016) 'Trained immunity: A program of innate immune memory in health and disease', Science 352(6284):aaf1098, DOI 10.1126/science.aaf1098.

merged_substrates.name: Intracellular — prion-conformational memory (CPEB / Orb2 functional amyloid)
merged_substrates.store_what: A self-perpetuating PROTEIN CONFORMATION as the bit: a protein switches soluble ↔ aggregated (amyloid), and the aggregated state templates its own propagation — a stable, replicable mark independent of DNA sequence. Characterized in neurons but mechanistically substrate-general.
merged_substrates.write_how: A trigger (serotonin-driven synaptic activity for CPEB/Orb2) nucleates the prion/amyloid conformation in the Q/N-rich low-complexity domain; existing aggregate seeds convert more monomer (self-templating write).
merged_substrates.read_how: The conformational state changes function — aggregated Orb2 flips from translational repressor to activator, locally sustaining the protein synthesis that maintains the synaptic change. The protein turns over but the state persists. Read = the functional output of whichever conformation is present.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Si, Lindquist & Kandel (2003) 'A Neuronal Isoform of the Aplysia CPEB Has Prion-Like Properties', Cell 115(7):879-891, DOI 10.1016/S0092-8674(03)01020-1 (PMID 14697205). In-vivo amyloid requirement: Majumdar et al. (2012) Cell 148(3):515-529, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2012.01.004. Cryo-EM: Hervás et al. (2020) Science 367:1230-1234, DOI 10.1126/science.aba3526.

merged_substrates.name: Intracellular — yeast Sup35 / [PSI+] prion (non-DNA phenotypic-state inheritance)
merged_substrates.store_what: The conformational state of the translation-termination factor Sup35 (soluble vs amyloid-like [PSI+] aggregate) as a heritable phenotypic memory of an inducing stress. ~1/3 of wild yeast strains carry prions; ~40% of induced traits were beneficial under tested conditions. (SONNET-unique; a second, non-neural prion exemplar.)
merged_substrates.write_how: Stress or stochastic fluctuation nucleates Sup35 monomers into an amyloid aggregate; the N-terminal prion domain self-templates — each new monomer contacting an aggregate adopts the same conformation.
merged_substrates.read_how: Hsp104 fragments aggregates and distributes them to daughters (mitotic transmission). [PSI+] cells read through stop codons less (Sup35 sequestered), revealing hidden genetic variation as new phenotypes; persists until cured (Hsp104 overexpression / guanidine).
merged_substrates.best_citation: Halfmann, Jarosz, Jones, Chang, Lancaster & Lindquist (2012) 'Prions are a common mechanism for phenotypic inheritance in wild yeasts', Nature 482(7385):363-368, DOI 10.1038/nature10875 (PMID 22337056; OA PMC3319070).

merged_substrates.name: Intracellular — bistable gene-regulatory / chromatin switches (synthetic + natural cellular memory)
merged_substrates.store_what: A stored discrete state (ON/OFF) held by a multistable gene-regulatory or chromatin circuit — a flip-flop / 'addressable cellular memory unit'. Spans the synthetic toggle, the natural lac hysteretic switch, and mitotically-heritable cell-identity chromatin states. This is where the attractor lens is the AUTHORS' OWN language.
merged_substrates.write_how: Synthetic toggle (Gardner 2000): two mutually-repressing genes; a transient chemical/thermal pulse flips which wins. Natural lac (Ozbudak 2004): positive feedback via permease LacY gives a hysteretic switch — inducer history sets the state. Cell-identity (Bruno/Del Vecchio 2022): a transient TF input tips a bistable chromatin circuit (auto/cross-catalysis of histone + DNA methyltransferases) with slow-erasure/fast-spreading time-scale separation giving hysteresis.
merged_substrates.read_how: The circuit's expression state is stably maintained without the original signal and inherited through divisions (DNMT1 / PRC2 maintenance); read by reporter/expression level. Hysteresis = present state depends on past exposure (memory).
merged_substrates.best_citation: Gardner, Cantor & Collins (2000) 'Construction of a genetic toggle switch in Escherichia coli', Nature 403:339-342, DOI 10.1038/35002131. Natural hysteresis: Ozbudak, Thattai, Lim, Shraiman & van Oudenaarden (2004) Nature 427:737-740, DOI 10.1038/nature02298. Chromatin cell-identity model: Bruno, Williams & Del Vecchio (2022) PLOS Comput. Biol. 18(4):e1009961, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009961 (OA).

merged_substrates.name: Intracellular / structural — centriole–centrosome template inheritance (non-DNA positional memory)
merged_substrates.store_what: Three-dimensional structural + positional information about centriole geometry and cell polarity, stored in the physical architecture of the mother centriole and its pericentriolar material — an explicitly non-sequence, structural-template store. (SONNET-unique.)
merged_substrates.write_how: The mother centriole templates the daughter: each new centriole nucleates orthogonally/adjacent to the mother and acquires its orientation/composition from the mother's structure — a physical templating event in S-phase, not a sequence write.
merged_substrates.read_how: At division, centrosomes organize the mitotic spindle; their orientation dictates the division axis and contributes to asymmetric fate (stem vs differentiating daughter); the mother centrosome is non-randomly segregated in asymmetric divisions, transmitting positional/polarity state.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Marshall (2009) 'Centriole inheritance', Prion 3(1):1-5, DOI 10.4161/pri.3.1.8789 (OA). (Confidence: medium — the structural-template framing is well-argued but the 'memory' read is partly interpretive.)

merged_substrates.name: Fungi — mycelial network directional / ecological growth memory
merged_substrates.store_what: A memory of growth direction and prior resource location, held in the network architecture: when relocated, regrowth is biased toward the side that previously faced a food bait — persisting even after the connecting cord is severed.
merged_substrates.write_how: Foraging toward a resource remodels the mycelial cord network into a directional anisotropy (and, at the tip, cytoskeletal/Spitzenkörper organization); the physical/structural asymmetry of the network is the write.
merged_substrates.read_how: On transfer to fresh substrate, regrowth emerges preferentially from the previously-resource-facing side — prior direction read off the surviving network structure (verified by destroying the cord first and still seeing biased regrowth).
merged_substrates.best_citation: Fukasawa, Savoury & Boddy (2020) 'Ecological memory and relocation decisions in fungal mycelial networks: responses to quantity and location of new resources', The ISME Journal 14(2):380-388, DOI 10.1038/s41396-019-0536-3 (OA PMC6976561).

merged_substrates.name: Placozoa — Trichoplax adhaerens peptidergic coordination (boundary case: coordination, not demonstrated storage)
merged_substrates.store_what: Caveat: NO retained engram is demonstrated. Trichoplax (NO neurons, NO synapses, NO muscles) coordinates behavior (feeding pauses, locomotion changes) via volume peptidergic signalling; whether it stores a lasting trace is open. Marks the FLOOR of the landscape.
merged_substrates.write_how: Chemosensory cells in the ventral epithelium secrete neuropeptide-like signals (e.g. endomorphin-like peptide) that induce neighbouring secretory cells to also secrete (peptide-induced peptide secretion / positive feedback), entraining the whole animal with no neural wiring.
merged_substrates.read_how: Peptides diffuse and reconfigure ciliary beating / body shape / feeding — a transient, diffusion-limited readout (e.g. a ciliary-arrest stopping wave); resumes once peptide degrades. No persistent recall shown.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Senatore, Reese & Smith (2017) 'Neuropeptidergic integration of behavior in Trichoplax adhaerens, an animal without synapses', J. Exp. Biol. 220:3381-3390, DOI 10.1242/jeb.162396 (OA). High cell-type diversity: Varoqueaux et al. (2018) Current Biology 28(21):3495-3501.e2, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2018.08.067.

merged_substrates.name: Ctenophore — independent (convergent) nervous-system origin (case study, not a storage substrate)
merged_substrates.store_what: Not a storage substrate per se — included for the landscape claim that neural-type processing tissue arose MORE THAN ONCE. Ctenophore neural systems lack many canonical bilaterian neurotransmitters/genes and use a unique syncytial nerve net, implying the 'neuron' is one convergent solution, not the unique seat of memory. No long-term habituation/learning is demonstrated in ctenophores.
merged_substrates.write_how: n/a — evolutionary/genomic evidence: distinct neurogenic gene complement; absent classical transmitters; syncytial (fused) nerve-net architecture.
merged_substrates.read_how: n/a — real-time behavioral integration (photoreception, prey capture, aboral-organ swimming) is observed; long-term storage is uncharacterized.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Moroz, Kocot, Citarella, … Kohn (2014) 'The ctenophore genome and the evolutionary origins of neural systems', Nature 510:109-114, DOI 10.1038/nature13400. Syncytial nerve net: Burkhardt, Colgren, … (Katz commentary) Science (2023) 'Syncytial nerve net in a ctenophore', DOI 10.1126/science.ade5645.

merged_substrates.name: Porifera — sponge (Ephydatia muelleri) contraction coordination without neurons (boundary case)
merged_substrates.store_what: A transient coordinated contraction state (the 'sneeze') propagated by glutamate/ATP paracrine signalling through P2X receptors. Short-term only: the refractory period after a contraction wave is the minimal stored state. NO habituation beyond the refractory period is demonstrated. Floor-marker. (SONNET-unique.)
merged_substrates.write_how: A mechanical/chemical stimulus releases glutamate → metabotropic glutamate receptors on contractile cells → ATP release → P2X receptors raise intracellular Ca2+, propagating the contraction wave (dual glutamate/ATP signalling).
merged_substrates.read_how: The refractory period following a full contraction cycle (canal system transiently unresponsive) is the read; no learning/habituation shown beyond this physiological refractoriness.
merged_substrates.best_citation: Ho, Goss & Leys (2025) 'ATP and glutamate coordinate contractions in the freshwater sponge Ephydatia muelleri', J. Exp. Biol. 228(3):JEB248010, DOI 10.1242/jeb.248010. (Confidence low: storage interpretation is minimal/contested.)

merged_landscape.cross_cutting_store_op:
LENS, NOT ASSERTED. No single physical store is shared across this landscape — and that is the point of an uncentered reading: memory is held in at least SIX physically distinct, non-privileged media, none of which is the 'real' one the others approximate. Enumerated without ranking: (1) ABSORBED/INTERNALIZED CHEMICAL — Physarum takes up and retains the repellent (sodium) as 'circulating memory' (Boussard 2019). (2) EXTERNALIZED or INTERNAL PHYSICAL STRUCTURE — Physarum's extracellular slime trail (Reid 2012) and its internal tube-diameter hierarchy (Kramar & Alim 2021); fungal cord/network anisotropy (Fukasawa 2020); centriole template geometry (Marshall 2009). (3) TRANSIENT IONIC / MEMBRANE-POTENTIAL STATE — flytrap cytosolic Ca2+ as a leaky-integrator count (Böhm 2016); bacterial biofilm K+ depolarization waves (Prindle 2015) and persistent imprinted K+ hyperpolarization (Yang/Bialecka-Fornal 2020); plant GLR wound waves (Lee & Seo 2022); Hydra bioelectric patterning. (4) CHROMATIN / EPIGENETIC MARK — vernalization H3K27me3 silencing of FLC (Yang/Dean 2017); H3K4me3 stress priming (Lämke 2017); trained-immunity histone marks (Netea 2016); bistable chromatin cell-identity circuits (Bruno 2022). (5) SEQUENCE / COPY-NUMBER in genome or cell population — CRISPR spacers as a dated archive (Barrangou 2007); clonal expansion + somatically-edited receptors in adaptive immunity (Lam/Farber 2024). (6) SELF-PERPETUATING MOLECULAR STATE — prion/amyloid conformation (CPEB/Orb2: Si 2003; yeast Sup35/[PSI+]: Halfmann 2012) and bistable gene-circuit attractors (Gardner 2000; Ozbudak 2004), where the 'bit' is which stable state the system has settled into.

The ONE abstract property that recurs across all six media — offered EXPLICITLY AS A LENS, NOT asserted as an established unifying mechanism — is MULTISTABILITY / SETTLING TO A PERSISTENT STATE: store = move the system into one of several self-maintaining configurations (a sodium load, a tube/cord geometry, a Ca2+ level above/below threshold, a silenced-vs-active chromatin state, a present-vs-absent spacer, an aggregated-vs-soluble protein, a flip-flop ON/OFF); read = let the system relax into / report the configuration it holds. The project's framework reading ('store = sculpt-the-attractor, read = relax-to-it') maps cleanly onto this.

CRITICAL DISCIPLINE (verified, and the decisive merge decision): the attractor framing is the cited AUTHORS' OWN language ONLY for the bistable-circuit (Gardner 2000 explicitly calls his toggle an 'addressable cellular memory unit' — verified; Ozbudak 2004's hysteresis), the prion cases (Si 2003; the self-templating-state framing), and transcriptional-network-as-learning-attractor models (Biswas, Clawson & Levin 2022, PMID 36613729). For the absorbed-chemical (Physarum sodium), externalized-slime/tube, ionic-integrator (flytrap), chromatin (vernalization/priming), sequence (CRISPR/immune), and structural-template (centriole) cases, the attractor description is THIS SYNTHESIS'S MAPPING, not the cited authors' framing — and it is a genuine STRETCH for the sequence/clonal cases (CRISPR spacer insertion, immune V-region selection) where a literal two-basin bistable landscape is not what the authors describe. So the landscape is held SUBSTRATE-PLURAL with the attractor lens laid over it, NOT collapsed under one asserted mechanism; and for Stentor (within-bout hierarchy disclaimed by its own authors as 'distinct from habituation/conditioning'), Trichoplax, sponge, and ctenophore even the existence of a stored trace is contested or undemonstrated.

UNCENTERED NOTE: the neuron does NOT sit at the center; it is one highly-salient fiber of a phenomenon in which 'retain-and-recall' is implemented by whatever persistent state a substrate can hold. THREE non-collapse axes keep any single example from grabbing privilege. FIRST, neural and aneural stores INTERLEAVE rather than nest: the box jellyfish does associative learning in a tiny rhopalial ganglion with NO central brain (Bielecki 2023), while a brainless slime mould does habituation with NO neurons at all (Boisseau 2016) — so 'has a brain', 'has neurons', and 'can store a memory' are three SEPARABLE axes. SECOND, the SAME molecular trick recurs on both sides of the neural/aneural line: the prion-conformational store (CPEB/Orb2) was characterized in neurons but is mechanistically identical to yeast Sup35 prions and to synthetic gene toggles — the substrate is 'a self-perpetuating molecular state', and the neuron is merely where one instance was studied. THIRD — the honest counterweight — naming many examples does NOT make them equally solid: the evidentiary WEIGHT is itself plural. The strongest, most unambiguous, addressable aneural stores are the molecular/chromatin/sequence ones (CRISPR, vernalization, immune memory, prion, bistable circuits) plus Physarum habituation; behavioral 'learning' claims for single cells and plants are genuinely contested (Gershman & Gunawardena 2021 eLife re-analysis; the Mimosa dispute, Biegler 2018), and Stentor's within-bout sequence is explicitly NOT habituation/conditioning per its own authors. So: storage IS substrate-plural and the neuron is one fiber — but so is the evidence, strongest where the store is a concrete molecular/structural state and weakest where it is inferred only from behavior. The 'settle-to-a-fixed-point' lens is the thread that lets all of these be seen at once WITHOUT making any one of them the template.

For the absorbed-chemical, slime/tube, ionic-integrator, chromatin, sequence, and structural-template substrates the attractor description is THIS SYNTHESIS'S mapping, NOT the authors' framing, and is a stretch for the CRISPR/immune sequence-store cases. merged_landscape.honest_tier: TWO-TIER, kept separate. TIER 1 = THE LITERATURE'S (biology). Every substrate triple (store_what / write_how / read_how) is a reported finding from peer-reviewed work, with each contested case marked IN-PLACE rather than dropped: Mimosa habituation is flagged DISPUTED (Gagliano 2014 vs Biegler 2018 motor-fatigue critique); Stentor's within-bout sequence is flagged as explicitly NOT habituation/conditioning per its own authors (Dexter 2019); Trichoplax (Placozoa), sponge (Porifera), and ctenophore are flagged as boundary/floor cases where a persistent stored trace is undemonstrated; and a dedicated skeptical-re-evaluation row (Gershman & Gunawardena 2021 eLife) is included so the survey is honest that single-cell 'learning' is contested. The strongest tier-1 stores (CRISPR, vernalization, adaptive + innate immune memory, prion CPEB/Sup35, bistable circuits, Physarum habituation) are concrete molecular/chromatin/sequence states; the weakest are inferred only from behavior. 13 of the heaviest-load citations were spot-verified on the web this pass (incl. both SONNET false attributions caught and the OPUS vernalization DOI corrected); two boundary-case citations (centriole, sponge) are marked unverifiable. TIER 2 = FRAMEWORK READING (the project's). The single universal store-op — 'store = sculpt-the-attractor, read = relax-to-it' (multistability / settling-to-a-fixed-point) — is the project's MFO / multistability lens laid OVER the landscape. It is NOT a demonstrated common physical mechanism: it is the cited authors' own language for only a subset of substrates (bistable circuits, prions, transcriptional-network learning) and is this synthesis's overlay for the rest. It is offered as a LENS that lets all six physically-distinct media be seen at once without privileging any one — explicitly un-asserted. NO LEANING: the union includes every substrate from EITHER survey (neither model privileged), weak/flagged citations are kept IN and marked, and the neuron is de-centered as one fiber among many with the evidentiary weight itself treated as plural.

opus_survey_meta.cross_cutting: No single physical store is shared across these substrates — and that is the point of an uncentered reading: the landscape stores memory in at least six physically distinct, NON-privileged media, none of which is 'the real one' that the others approximate. Enumerated without ranking: (1) ABSORBED/INTERNALIZED CHEMICAL — Physarum literally takes up and retains the repellent (sodium) as a 'circulating memory' (Boussard 2019). (2) EXTERNALIZED PHYSICAL STRUCTURE — Physarum's extracellular slime trail and transport-tube thickness gradient hold a spatial map OUTSIDE the cell (Reid 2012); fungal cord/network anisotropy holds growth direction (Fukasawa 2020). (3) TRANSIENT IONIC / MEMBRANE-POTENTIAL STATE — flytrap cytosolic Ca2+ as a leaky-integrator count (Böhm/Hedrich 2016); bacterial biofilm K+ depolarization waves (Prindle 2015); cnidarian/Hydra bioelectric patterning state. (4) CHROMATIN / EPIGENETIC MARK — vernalization H3K27me3 silencing of FLC, mitotically heritable (Bastow 2004; Angel 2011); trained-immunity histone marks (Netea 2016). (5) SEQUENCE / COPY-NUMBER in the genome or cell population — CRISPR spacers as a literal dated archive (Barrangou 2007); clonal expansion + somatically-edited receptors in adaptive immunity (Lam/Farber 2024). (6) SELF-PERPETUATING MOLECULAR STATE — prion/amyloid conformation (CPEB/Orb2; Si 2003, Majumdar 2012) and bistable gene-circuit attractors (Gardner 2000; Ozbudak 2004), where the 'bit' is which stable state the system has settled into. \n\nThe one ABSTRACT property that recurs across all six media — offered explicitly as a LENS, not asserted as an established unifying mechanism — is MULTISTABILITY / SETTLING TO A PERSISTENT STATE. In every case 'store' = move the system into one of several self-maintaining configurations (a sodium load, a tube/cord geometry, a Ca2+ level above/below threshold, a silenced-vs-active chromatin state, a present-vs-absent spacer, an aggregated-vs-soluble protein, a flip-flop's ON/OFF), and 'read' = let the system relax into / report the configuration it is holding. The framework reading ('store = sculpt-the-attractor, read = relax-to-it') maps cleanly onto this — and the literature already speaks this language for the bistable-circuit and prion cases (Gardner 2000's 'addressable cellular memory unit'; Ozbudak 2004's hysteresis; Biswas/Clawson/Levin 2022 model transcriptional networks as learning attractor systems, PMID 36613729). But the attractor framing is a description of dynamics that the authors themselves use only for SOME substrates; it is NOT a demonstrated common physical mechanism, and for Stentor and Trichoplax even the existence of a stored trace is contested/undemonstrated.
opus_survey_meta.uncentered_note: Holding all perspectives at once, the neuron does NOT sit at the center: it is one highly-salient fiber of a broader phenomenon in which 'retain-and-recall' is implemented by whatever persistent state a substrate can hold. Three observations keep any single example from grabbing privilege. FIRST, neural and aneural stores INTERLEAVE rather than nest: the box jellyfish does associative learning in a tiny rhopalial ganglion with NO central brain (Bielecki 2023), while a brainless slime mould does habituation with NO neurons at all (Boisseau 2016) — so 'has a brain', 'has neurons', and 'can store a memory' are three separable axes, and centering on neurons would hide the first two. SECOND, the SAME molecular trick recurs on both sides of the neural/aneural line: the prion-conformational store (CPEB/Orb2) was characterized in neurons but is mechanistically identical to yeast prions and synthetic gene toggles — the substrate is 'a self-perpetuating molecular state', and the neuron is merely where one instance was studied. Chromatin memory (vernalization) and CRISPR are flat-out non-neural and arguably the most UNAMBIGUOUS, addressable memories in the whole survey. THIRD — the honest counterweight — naming many examples does not make them all equally solid: the most robust aneural stores are the molecular/chromatin/sequence ones (CRISPR, vernalization, immune memory, prion, bistable circuits: high confidence) and Physarum habituation; behavioral 'learning' claims for single cells and plants are genuinely contested (Gershman/Gunawardena 2021 eLife re-analysis; the Mimosa habituation dispute, Biegler 2018), and Stentor's sequential logic is explicitly NOT habituation/conditioning per its own authors. So the uncentered frame is: storage IS substrate-plural and the neuron is one fiber of it — but the evidentiary WEIGHT is plural too, strongest where the store is a concrete molecular/structural state and weakest where it is inferred only from behavior. The 'settle-to-a-fixed-point' lens is offered as the thread that lets all of these be seen at once without making any one of them the template.

sonnet_survey_meta.cross_cutting:
Across every substrate surveyed, a single abstract pattern recurs regardless of molecular implementation: storage = sculpt the attractor; recall = relax toward it.

In the tube-diameter hierarchy of Physarum, the attractor is the flow equilibrium that routes cytoplasm toward food. In the FLC chromatin locus, the attractor is the H3K27me3-silenced transcriptional state. In CRISPR arrays, it is the spacer-indexed guide-RNA–Cas complex that cleaves a matching invader. In memory B cells, it is the V-region sequence that matches the antigen. In the CPEB prion, it is the self-templating amyloid conformation that locally activates translation. In the Sup35/[PSI+] switch, it is the aggregated vs. soluble protein basin. In the bistable chromatin circuit, it is the mutually reinforcing histone/DNA methylation state.

In every case: (1) a perturbation event reshapes a landscape that has at least two stable basins; (2) the reshaped landscape persists after the perturbation is removed; (3) a subsequent stimulus drives the system back to the sculpted basin, producing a response that differs from the naive response — this difference is the read-out of memory.

The mechanisms that implement 'sculpt' span: mechanical/structural remodelling (tube walls, cord density, centriole template), chemical accumulation (sodium in Physarum, Ca2+ in Venus flytrap), covalent chromatin marks (H3K27me3, H3K4me3, DNA methylation), protein-conformation self-templating (CPEB, Sup35), sequence insertion into a polymer (CRISPR spacers), clonal cell selection with somatic mutation (immune memory), and membrane-potential hyperpolarisation (bacterial K+ channel memory). The list is substrate-heterogeneous but the abstract storage logic is not.
sonnet_survey_meta.uncentered_note: The neuron is a high-throughput, specialised implementation of the sculpt-attractor write/relax-to-it read logic — it is not the originator of that logic. The survey above finds the same abstract operation in: a single-celled amoeba (Physarum), a bacterium (CRISPR, K+ channel), a fungal network, a plant (FLC, GLR wave, Venus flytrap Ca2+ counter, stress priming), a single ciliate (Stentor), a prion-like protein (CPEB, Sup35), a chromatin circuit, an immune cell lineage, and a neuron-free animal (Trichoplax). Each of these is a fibre in the full landscape of memory substrates; no single fibre is the 'real' mechanism. The neuron appears salient only because vertebrate neuroscience has dominated the study of memory for historical and practical reasons, not because neurons are privileged physical substrates for the abstract operation. This survey holds that frame deliberately uncentered.
